source.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לָמ֑וּת וַיָּב֣וֹא אֵ֠לָיו יְשַׁעְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־אָמ֜וֹץ הַנָּבִ֗יא וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ צַ֣ו לְבֵיתֶ֔ךָ כִּ֛י מֵ֥ת אַתָּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִֽחְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In the days those became sick Hezekiah to die, and came to him Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet and said to him, thus says Yahweh: command to your household, for dying you [are] and not you will live.

en.L: In those days Hezekiah became sick to [the point of] dying, and Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, came to him and said to him, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Give command to your household, for you are dying, and you will not live."
en.B: In those days Hezekiah fell ill and was close to death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Give final instructions to your household, for you are dying and will not live."
en.R: Around that time Hezekiah became so sick that he was about to die. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to see him. He said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Tell your family what they must do after you are gone. You are going to die. You will not get well."

es.L: En aquellos días Ezequías enfermó de muerte, y vino a él el profeta Isaías hijo de Amoz y le dijo: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Da órdenes a tu casa, porque vas a morir y no vivirás».
es.B: En aquellos días Ezequías cayó enfermo y estuvo a punto de morir. El profeta Isaías hijo de Amoz fue a verlo y le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Da tus últimas instrucciones a tu familia, porque vas a morir; no vivirás».
es.R: Por aquel tiempo Ezequías se enfermó tanto que estaba a punto de morir. El profeta Isaías hijo de Amoz fue a verlo. Le dijo: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Dile a tu familia lo que deben hacer cuando ya no estés. Vas a morir. No te vas a sanar».

fr.L: En ces jours-là, Ézéchias fut malade à en mourir, et Isaïe fils d’Amots, le prophète, vint auprès de lui et lui dit : « Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Donne tes ordres à ta maison, car tu vas mourir, et tu ne vivras pas. »
fr.B: En ce temps-là, Ézéchias tomba malade et fut sur le point de mourir. Le prophète Isaïe, fils d’Amots, vint le voir et lui dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Donne tes dernières instructions à ta famille, car tu vas mourir ; tu ne vivras pas. »
fr.R: À cette époque, Ézéchias est tombé tellement malade qu’il allait mourir. Le prophète Isaïe fils d’Amots est venu le voir. Il lui a dit : « Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Dis à ta famille ce qu’elle devra faire après ta mort. Tu vas mourir. Tu ne guériras pas. »

sw.L: Katika siku hizo Hezekia aliugua [karibu] kufa, naye Isaya mwana wa Amozi, nabii, akaja kwake, akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Toa maagizo kwa watu wa nyumba yako, kwa maana unakufa, wala hutaishi."
sw.B: Siku hizo Hezekia aliugua, akakaribia kufa. Nabii Isaya mwana wa Amozi akaja kwake, akamwambia, "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Toa maagizo yako ya mwisho kwa watu wa nyumba yako, kwa maana unakufa, wala hutapona."
sw.R: Wakati huo Hezekia aliugua sana hata akakaribia kufa. Nabii Isaya mwana wa Amozi akaja kumwona. Akasema, "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Waambie watu wa familia yako yale watakayopaswa kufanya baada ya wewe kuondoka. Utakufa. Hutapona."

vi.L: Trong những ngày ấy, Ê-xê-chia lâm bệnh gần chết. Nhà tiên tri Ê-sai con trai A-mốt đến gặp vua và nói với vua: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Hãy truyền lệnh cho nhà vua, vì vua sắp chết, không sống được nữa."
vi.B: Trong những ngày ấy, Ê-xê-chia lâm bệnh nặng gần chết. Nhà tiên tri Ê-sai con trai A-mốt đến gặp vua và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Hãy dặn dò người nhà lần cuối, vì vua sắp chết, không sống được nữa."
vi.R: Khoảng thời gian ấy, Ê-xê-chia bệnh nặng đến nỗi sắp chết. Nhà tiên tri Ê-sai con trai A-mốt đến thăm vua. Ông nói: "Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Hãy dặn gia đình vua những việc họ phải làm sau khi vua qua đời. Vua sắp chết rồi. Vua sẽ không khỏi bệnh."

ko.L: 그 날들에 히스기야가 병들어 죽게 되었다. 그러자 아모스의 아들 예언자 이사야가 그에게 와서 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하십니다. '네 집안에 명령을 내려라. 네가 죽고 살지 못할 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그 무렵 히스기야가 병이 들어 죽게 되었다. 아모스의 아들 예언자 이사야가 그에게 와서 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하십니다. '네 집안일을 정리하여라. 네가 죽을 것이고 살지 못할 것이다.'"
ko.R: 그 무렵 히스기야가 병이 들어 거의 죽게 되었다. 아모스의 아들 예언자 이사야가 그를 찾아와서 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀입니다. '네가 죽은 뒤에 네 가족이 할 일을 일러 두어라. 너는 죽을 것이다. 병이 낫지 않을 것이다.'"

pt.L: Naqueles dias Ezequias adoeceu a ponto de morrer, e Isaías, filho de Amoz, o profeta, veio a ele e lhe disse: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Põe a tua casa em ordem, porque tu estás morrendo e não viverás."
pt.B: Naqueles dias Ezequias ficou doente e esteve à beira da morte. O profeta Isaías, filho de Amoz, foi até ele e disse: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Põe a tua casa em ordem, porque estás morrendo e não vais viver."
pt.R: Nessa época, Ezequias ficou tão doente que estava quase morrendo. O profeta Isaías, filho de Amoz, foi visitá-lo. Ele disse: "É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Explica à tua família o que ela deve fazer quando morreres. Vais morrer. Não vais ficar bom."

decisions.choice: in those days: during the years of Sennacherib's threat to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The phrase ties the illness loosely to the events of chapters 36-37. Verse 6 still promises rescue from the king of Assyria, so the illness came before that danger had ended. The same account is told in 2 Kings 20:1-11, and more briefly in 2 Chronicles 32:24.

decisions.choice: give command to your household: settle your affairs and give your last instructions before death
decisions.reason: The same words are said to Ahithophel before he dies (2 Samuel 17:23). A dying man told his family how his goods and duties were to be handled.

decisions.choice: you are dying, and you will not live: death is near and the illness will not be cured
decisions.reason: The participle describes death as already on its way. The second clause says the same thing again from the other side: Hezekiah will not recover. Verse 5 shows that the sentence could still be turned back in answer to prayer.

decisions.choice: Tell your family what they must do after you are gone
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what the idiom means (m2).

decisions.choice: the wording of 2 Kings 20:1-11, shortened
decisions.reason: Isaiah 38:1-8 tells more briefly what 2 Kings 20:1-11 tells; the published Swahili of 2 Kings is kept where the Hebrew is the same, and left out or changed where Isaiah has less or other words.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2 Kings 20:1 reused at each level
decisions.reason: Isaiah 38:1-8 and 21-22 tell the events of 2 Kings 20:1-11 in a shorter form; as the terms note sets, the published 2 Kings wording is reused where the Hebrew is the same and changed where it differs.

decisions.choice: Verses 1-8 and 21-22 reuse the published Korean of 2 Kings 20:1-11, changing only where the Hebrew of Isaiah differs; the prophet speaks to the king in 합쇼체 and God's words inside in 해라체
decisions.reason: The terms note sets the parallel, and the address forms of 2 Kings 20:1. Hezekiah's poem (verses 9-20) is found only in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: the Portuguese of 2 Kings 20:1-11 reused where the Hebrew is the same; Põe a tua casa em ordem (L, B)
decisions.reason: Verses 1-8 and 21-22 tell what 2 Kings 20:1-11 tells, in shorter form, so each level keeps 2 Kings' Portuguese wherever the Hebrew agrees: "Põe a tua casa em ordem" for the idiom (m2), Hezekiah's prayer with "lembra-te", "um bolo de figos", and "a sombra ... dez degraus" on "os degraus de Acaz". Isaiah's Hebrew differs in verses 4-8: the word comes to Isaiah without the courtyard, God says "Vai" and adds fifteen years without the third day, and the sign is part of the LORD's own message, so it is said to Hezekiah with "tu" (verse 7), where 2 Kings 20:9 has Isaiah speak with "você". The psalm of verses 9-20 is not in Kings.

decisions.choice: turned his face to the wall: turned away from the people in the room to pray alone
decisions.reason: Lying on his sickbed, the king turns away from those around him. The act shows that his prayer is private and earnest, not that he turns from God (compare 1 Kings 21:4, where Ahab turns his face away in sulking).

source.text: וַיֹּאמַ֗ר אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ זְכָר־נָ֞א אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לְפָנֶ֗יךָ בֶּֽאֱמֶת֙ וּבְלֵ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם וְהַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עָשִׂ֑יתִי וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכִ֥י גָדֽוֹל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he said, please, Yahweh, remember please how I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a heart whole, and the good in your eyes I have done. And wept Hezekiah weeping great.

en.L: And he said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember, please, how I have walked before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and [that] I have done what [is] good in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes." And Hezekiah wept [with] great weeping.
en.B: He said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember how I have lived before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} faithfully and with an undivided heart, doing what is good in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight." And Hezekiah wept loudly.
en.R: He said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please remember how I have always been faithful to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I have served {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all my heart. I have done what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see as good." Then Hezekiah cried very hard.

es.L: Y dijo: «Te ruego, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, acuérdate, te ruego, de cómo he andado delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} con fidelidad y con corazón íntegro, y he hecho lo bueno ante {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos». Y lloró Ezequías con gran llanto.
es.B: Dijo: «Te ruego, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que recuerdes cómo he vivido delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} con fidelidad y con un corazón entero, haciendo lo que es bueno a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos». Y Ezequías lloró amargamente.
es.R: Dijo: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, por favor, recuerda que siempre te he sido fiel. Te he servido con todo mi corazón. He hecho lo que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} consideras bueno». Luego Ezequías lloró desconsoladamente.

fr.L: Et il dit : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} donc que j’ai marché devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} avec fidélité et d’un cœur entier, et que j’ai fait ce qui [est] bien à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} yeux. » Et Ézéchias pleura abondamment.
fr.B: Il dit : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que j’ai vécu devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} avec fidélité et d’un cœur sans partage, et que j’ai fait ce qui est bien à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} yeux. » Et Ézéchias pleura à chaudes larmes.
fr.R: Il a dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai toujours été fidèle. Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai servi de tout mon cœur. J’ai fait ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} trouves bien. » Puis Ézéchias a beaucoup pleuré.

sw.L: Akasema, "Tafadhali, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kumbuka, tafadhali, jinsi nilivyoenenda mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kwa uaminifu na kwa moyo mkamilifu, na [kwamba] nimefanya yaliyo mema machoni {{deity_pronoun:pako|Pako}}." Naye Hezekia akalia kilio kikuu.
sw.B: Akasema, "Tafadhali, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kumbuka jinsi nilivyoishi mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kwa uaminifu na kwa moyo usiogawanyika, nikifanya yaliyo mema machoni {{deity_pronoun:pako|Pako}}." Naye Hezekia akalia kwa sauti kubwa.
sw.R: Akasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali kumbuka jinsi ambavyo nimekuwa mwaminifu {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}} siku zote. Nimekutumikia kwa moyo wangu wote. Nimefanya yale unayoyaona kuwa mema." Kisha Hezekia akalia sana.

vi.L: Vua thưa: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin Ngài nhớ lại con đã bước đi trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong sự trung tín và với một tấm lòng trọn vẹn, và đã làm điều tốt lành trước mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}." Rồi Ê-xê-chia khóc lớn.
vi.B: Vua thưa: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhớ lại con đã sống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cách trung tín, với một lòng không chia hai, và đã làm điều tốt lành trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}." Rồi Ê-xê-chia khóc lớn.
vi.R: Vua thưa: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhớ lại con đã luôn trung thành với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Con đã hết lòng phục vụ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Con đã làm điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy là tốt." Rồi Ê-xê-chia khóc nức nở.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 말했다. "아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 주님 앞에서 진실하게, 온전한 마음으로 걸었고, 주님의 눈에 좋은 일을 한 것을 부디 기억해 주십시오." 그리고 히스기야가 크게 울며 울었다.
ko.B: 그가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 주님 앞에서 진실하게, 한결같은 마음으로 살아왔고, 주님 보시기에 선한 일을 해 온 것을 부디 기억해 주십시오." 그리고 히스기야는 큰 소리로 울었다.
ko.R: 그가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 늘 주님께 충성해 온 것을 부디 기억해 주십시오. 저는 온 마음으로 주님을 섬겼습니다. 저는 주님께서 좋게 보시는 일을 했습니다." 그러고 나서 히스기야는 몹시 울었다.

pt.L: E disse: "Por favor, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, lembra-te, por favor, de como andei diante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} com fidelidade e com coração íntegro, e [de que] fiz o que [é] bom aos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} olhos." E Ezequias chorou [com] grande choro.
pt.B: Ele disse: "Por favor, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, lembra-te de como vivi diante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} com fidelidade e de coração inteiro, fazendo o que é bom aos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} olhos." E Ezequias chorou muito alto.
pt.R: Ele disse: "{{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, por favor, lembra-te de que sempre fui fiel a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} servi de todo o coração. Fiz o que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} consideras bom." Então Ezequias chorou muito.

decisions.choice: walked before you: lived my whole life in your presence and service
decisions.reason: To walk before God is to live in his sight and serve him (Genesis 17:1; 1 Kings 2:4). Hezekiah does not claim to be sinless (verse 17 speaks of his sins); he appeals to a life of loyalty.

decisions.choice: in faithfulness and with a whole heart: with steady loyalty and undivided devotion
decisions.reason: The word for faithfulness is the same one Hezekiah uses of God in verses 18-19. A whole (complete) heart is one not split between God and other loyalties (1 Kings 8:61; 2 Kings 20:3).

decisions.choice: I have always been faithful to you. I have served you with all my heart.
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the prayer into short sentences and explains the idiom of walking before God (m1).

records.literal_gloss: Go and you will say to Hezekiah, thus says Yahweh the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears; here I [am] adding to your days fifteen years.

en.L: "Go and say to Hezekiah, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look, I am adding fifteen years to your days.
en.B: "Go and say to Hezekiah, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestor David, says this: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Now I will add fifteen years to your days.
en.R: "Go and tell Hezekiah, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says, the God your ancestor David served: I have heard your prayer, and I have seen you crying. So I will let you live fifteen more years.

es.L: «Ve y di a Ezequías: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de David tu padre: He oído tu oración; he visto tus lágrimas. He aquí que yo añado a tus días quince años.
es.B: «Ve y dile a Ezequías: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de tu antepasado David, dice esto: He oído tu oración; he visto tus lágrimas. Añadiré quince años a tu vida.
es.R: «Ve y dile a Ezequías: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios a quien sirvió tu antepasado David: He oído tu oración y he visto tus lágrimas. Por eso te dejaré vivir quince años más.

fr.L: « Va, et dis à Ézéchias : “Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de David ton père : J’ai entendu ta prière, j’ai vu tes larmes. Voici, j’ajoute à tes jours quinze ans.
fr.B: « Va dire à Ézéchias : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de ton ancêtre David, dit ceci : J’ai entendu ta prière, j’ai vu tes larmes. Je vais ajouter quinze années à tes jours.
fr.R: « Va dire à Ézéchias : “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu que ton ancêtre David a servi : J’ai entendu ta prière et je t’ai vu pleurer. Alors je vais te laisser vivre encore quinze ans.

sw.L: "Nenda ukamwambie Hezekia, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi, Mungu wa Daudi baba yako: Nimeyasikia maombi yako; nimeyaona machozi yako. Tazama, ninaziongeza siku zako miaka kumi na mitano.
sw.B: "Nenda ukamwambie Hezekia, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa babu yako Daudi, asema hivi: Nimeyasikia maombi yako; nimeyaona machozi yako. Sasa nitakuongezea miaka kumi na mitano ya kuishi.
sw.R: "Nenda ukamwambie Hezekia, 'Hiki ndicho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu aliyetumikiwa na babu yako Daudi, anachosema: Nimeyasikia maombi yako, nami nimekuona ukilia. Kwa hiyo nitakuacha uishi miaka kumi na mitano zaidi.

vi.L: "Hãy đi và nói với Ê-xê-chia: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Đa-vít tổ phụ ngươi, phán thế này: Ta đã nghe lời cầu nguyện của ngươi; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy nước mắt ngươi. Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ thêm cho ngươi mười lăm năm.

vi.R: "Hãy đi nói với Ê-xê-chia: 'Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời mà Đa-vít tổ tiên con đã phục vụ, phán: Ta đã nghe lời con cầu nguyện, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy con khóc. Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cho con sống thêm mười lăm năm nữa.

ko.L: "가서 히스기야에게 말하여라. '네 조상 다윗의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 이와 같이 말한다. 내가 네 기도를 들었고 네 눈물을 보았다. 보아라, 내가 네 날들에 15년을 더하겠다.

ko.R: "가서 히스기야에게 전하여라. '네 조상 다윗이 섬긴 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 하는 말이다. 내가 네 기도를 들었고, 네가 우는 것을 보았다. 그러니 내가 너를 15년 더 살게 하겠다.

pt.L: "Vai e diz a Ezequias: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Davi, teu pai: Ouvi a tua oração; vi as tuas lágrimas. Eis que eu acrescento aos teus dias quinze anos.
pt.B: "Vai e diz a Ezequias: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus do teu antepassado Davi: Ouvi a tua oração; vi as tuas lágrimas. Agora vou acrescentar quinze anos aos teus dias.
pt.R: "Vai e diz a Ezequias: 'É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz, o Deus a quem o teu antepassado Davi serviu: Ouvi a tua oração e vi o teu choro. Por isso vou deixar que vivas mais quinze anos.

decisions.choice: David your father: David your ancestor
decisions.reason: David lived about three hundred years before Hezekiah. Calling God the God of David reminds Hezekiah of the promise made to David's line (2 Samuel 7:16), which verse 6 goes on to apply to the city.

decisions.choice: here I am adding: the promise is as good as done
decisions.reason: The particle with a participle announces what God is about to do. The fifteen years fit the history: Hezekiah's illness came about 701 BC, and his reign ended about 686 BC.

decisions.choice: the God your ancestor David served
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title "God of David" by saying David served him.

decisions.choice: "thêm cho ngươi mười lăm năm" right after the tears
alternatives: the 2 Kings 20:5 lines on healing and the third day
decisions.reason: Isaiah moves straight from the tears to the fifteen years; the 2 Kings wording is kept for the shared words and the lines Isaiah lacks are left out. God says "ngươi" (L) and "con" (B, R) to Hezekiah.

decisions.choice: God names himself without the honorific ("하나님 주(야훼)가 이와 같이 말한다")
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 20:5: God dictates the message Isaiah is to give, so the self-reference has no "-시-". Isaiah's text has no "turn back", no "ruler of my people" and no healing on the third day; the 2 Kings wording is shortened to match.

decisions.choice: the sign: a visible event that guarantees the promise
decisions.reason: A sign is something God does that can be seen, given to confirm a word that has not yet come true (7:11, 14; 37:30). Here God offers it; in 2 Kings 20:8-10 Hezekiah asks for it and chooses which way the shadow will move. Verse 22 of this chapter records his request.

decisions.choice: God's message continues in the first person through verse 8, without Kings' question to Hezekiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah's Hebrew gives the sign directly, so the French of 2 Kings is reused only where the words are the same.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" (L); "con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings Isaiah himself speaks to the king and says "vua"; here the words are still the LORD's message (verses 5-8), so they keep God's "ngươi" / "con".

decisions.choice: "주(야훼)가 ... 이룰 것이라는", without the honorific
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings these words are Isaiah's to the king; in Isaiah they are still the LORD's message (verses 5-8), so God speaks of himself in the plain style.

decisions.choice: para ti, o teu sinal, te (tu)
alternatives: para você, o seu sinal (as 2 Kings 20:9)
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 20:9 Isaiah offers the sign in his own voice and says "você" to the king; here the sign is part of the LORD's message that began in verse 5, so the LORD speaks to Hezekiah with "tu", as he does to one person throughout.

fr.L: Voici, je fais reculer l’ombre sur les degrés, celle qui est descendue sur les degrés d’Achaz avec le soleil, de dix degrés en arrière.” » Et le soleil recula de dix degrés sur les degrés qu’il avait descendus.
fr.B: Voici : l’ombre que le soleil a fait descendre sur les marches d’Achaz, je vais la faire reculer de dix marches.” » Et le soleil recula de dix marches sur les marches qu’il avait descendues.
fr.R: Le soleil a fait descendre une ombre sur l’escalier d’Achaz. Écoute ! Je vais faire remonter cette ombre de dix marches.” » Et la lumière du soleil est bien remontée de dix des marches qu’elle avait descendues.

sw.L: Tazama, ninakirudisha kivuli katika ngazi, kilichoshuka katika ngazi za Ahazi pamoja na jua, nyuma hatua kumi.'" Nalo jua likarudi hatua kumi katika ngazi lilizokuwa limeshuka.
sw.B: Tazama, nitakifanya kivuli ambacho jua limekishusha katika ngazi za Ahazi kirudi nyuma hatua kumi.'" Kisha jua likarudi nyuma hatua kumi katika ngazi lilizokuwa limeshuka.
sw.R: Jua limefanya kivuli kishuke katika ngazi za Ahazi. Tazama! Nitakifanya kivuli hicho kirudi juu hatua kumi.'" Na kweli mwanga wa jua ulirudi juu hatua kumi kati ya zile ulizokuwa umeshuka.

vi.L: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ khiến bóng trên các bậc, là bóng mặt trời đã đi xuống trên cầu thang của A-cha, lùi lại mười bậc.'" Và mặt trời lùi lại mười bậc trên các bậc nó đã đi xuống.
vi.B: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ khiến bóng nắng mà mặt trời đã đưa xuống trên các bậc cầu thang của A-cha lùi lại mười bậc.'" Bấy giờ mặt trời lùi lại mười bậc trên các bậc mà nó đã đi xuống.
vi.R: Mặt trời đã làm cho một cái bóng đi xuống cầu thang của A-cha. Hãy xem! Ta sẽ khiến bóng ấy lùi lên mười bậc.'" Và bóng nắng quả thật đã lùi lên mười bậc mà nó đã đi xuống.

ko.L: 보아라, 해와 함께 아하스의 계단 위로 내려간 계단의 그림자를 내가 열 계단 뒤로 물러가게 하겠다.'" 그러자 해가 내려갔던 계단에서 열 계단을 물러갔다.
ko.B: 보아라, 해가 아하스의 계단에 드리운 그림자를 내가 열 계단 뒤로 물러가게 하겠다.'" 그러자 해가 내려갔던 계단에서 열 계단 뒤로 물러갔다.
ko.R: 해가 아하스의 계단에 그림자를 드리워 그것이 내려갔다. 보아라! 내가 그 그림자를 열 계단 위로 다시 올라가게 하겠다.'" 그러자 정말로 햇빛이 내려갔던 계단에서 열 계단을 다시 올라갔다.

pt.L: Eis que eu faço voltar a sombra nos degraus, que desceu nos degraus de Acaz com o sol, dez degraus para trás.'" E o sol voltou dez degraus nos degraus que tinha descido.
pt.B: Vou fazer a sombra que o sol fez descer pelos degraus de Acaz voltar dez degraus.'" Então o sol voltou dez degraus nos degraus por onde tinha descido.
pt.R: O sol fez uma sombra descer pela escadaria de Acaz. Olha! Vou fazer essa sombra voltar dez degraus para cima.'" E a luz do sol de fato voltou dez dos degraus que tinha descido.

decisions.choice: the steps of Ahaz: a stairway built by Ahaz, on which the moving shadow showed the time of day
decisions.reason: The word means steps or stairs. As the sun moved, a shadow crept down the stairs, marking the hours. Some take the steps as the markings of a sundial; either way the shadow moved backward, against the course of the day. Ahaz was Hezekiah's father.

decisions.choice: the steps of Ahaz: the Masoretic reading
alternatives: the steps of the upper room of Ahaz
decisions.reason: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads "the steps of the upper room of Ahaz", recalling the upper room of Ahaz in 2 Kings 23:12. The Masoretic text is kept.

decisions.choice: the sun went back: the sun's shadow moved back, as the sign promised
decisions.reason: The narrative says the sun itself went back, because the shadow moves with the sun. 2 Kings 20:11 says the LORD brought the shadow back after Isaiah cried out to him. The text does not say how the sign was worked.

decisions.choice: The sun has made a shadow go down the stairway of Ahaz. Look! I will make that shadow go back up ten steps.
decisions.reason: Readable first describes the shadow, then the promise, and says "sunlight" for the sun (m3).

decisions.choice: a sombra; os degraus de Acaz (L, B), a escadaria de Acaz (R)
alternatives: o relógio de sol de Acaz
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 20:9-11 in Portuguese: the shadow moves on a stairway (m1), so every level speaks of "a sombra" and "degraus", the steps of a stair; "relógio de sol" would say more than the Hebrew does.

vi.R: Ê-xê-chia vua Giu-đa đã viết bài này sau khi vua bị bệnh và được lành:

ko.B: 유다 왕 히스기야가 병들었다가 그 병에서 회복된 뒤에 쓴 글.
ko.R: 유다 왕 히스기야는 병이 들었다가 나은 뒤에 이 글을 썼다.

pt.B: Texto escrito por Ezequias, rei de Judá, depois de ter ficado doente e se recuperado da sua doença:

decisions.choice: a writing: a written composition, here a poem of lament and thanks
decisions.reason: The word normally means something written, such as a letter or document (2 Chronicles 21:12). Because the poem resembles a psalm, some suggest the word should be read with one letter different as miktam, a term found in the titles of Psalms 16 and 56-60. The consonants of the text give "writing".

decisions.choice: the poem appears only in Isaiah
decisions.reason: The account in 2 Kings 20 has no poem. Isaiah places Hezekiah's own words between the sign (verses 7-8) and the note about the figs (verses 21-22).

decisions.choice: when he was sick and lived: the poem looks back on the illness from after the recovery
decisions.reason: Verses 10-14 recall what he felt while near death; verses 15-20 give thanks for his healing.

decisions.choice: Escrito
decisions.reason: Hezekiah's poem has no parallel in 2 Kings and is drafted fresh, in lines as the English, with God addressed as "tú".

decisions.choice: Hezekiah's poem (verses 10-20) is speech: the passé composé for the past, "tu" to God
alternatives: the passé simple of the narrative
decisions.reason: As the terms note for prayers and laments; the narrative frame of chapters 36-39 keeps the passé simple at L and B.

decisions.choice: In the poem Hezekiah speaks to God in 합쇼체 with "저" and "주님" (verses 12-14, 16-19) and about God in the plain style with the honorific (verses 15, 20); his own words of despair in verses 10-11 are in the plain style
decisions.reason: As the Korean psalms: prayer to God is 합쇼체, speaking about God is the plain style; the poem moves between the two, as the Hebrew moves between "you" and "he".

source.text: אֲנִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי בִּדְמִ֥י יָמַ֛י אֵלֵ֖כָה בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֣י שְׁא֑וֹל פֻּקַּ֖דְתִּי יֶ֥תֶר שְׁנוֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I said, in the half of my days let me go in the gates of Sheol; I have been deprived [of] the rest of my years.

en.L: I said, "In the middle of my days I must go into the gates of Sheol; \q I am deprived of the rest of my years."
en.B: I said, "At the midpoint of my days I must go into the gates of Sheol; \q I am robbed of the years that remain to me."
en.R: I said, "I am only halfway through my life, and I must go through the gates of the grave. \q The rest of my years have been taken from me."

es.L: Yo dije: «En la mitad de mis días he de irme a las puertas del Seol; \q privado soy del resto de mis años».
es.B: Yo dije: «En la mitad de mis días tengo que ir a las puertas del lugar de los muertos; \q me han robado los años que me quedaban».
es.R: Yo dije: «Solo he vivido la mitad de mi vida, y ya debo pasar por las puertas del lugar de los muertos. \q Me han quitado el resto de mis años».

fr.L: J’ai dit : « Au milieu de mes jours, je dois m’en aller aux portes du Shéol ; \q je suis privé du reste de mes années. »
fr.B: J’ai dit : « À la moitié de mes jours, je dois franchir les portes du séjour des morts ; \q on me vole les années qui me restaient. »
fr.R: J’ai dit : « Je ne suis qu’à la moitié de ma vie, et je dois passer les portes du séjour des morts. \q Le reste de mes années m’a été enlevé. »

sw.L: Nilisema, "Katikati ya siku zangu ni lazima niende katika malango ya Kuzimu; \q nimenyimwa miaka yangu iliyobaki."
sw.B: Nilisema, "Katikati ya siku za maisha yangu ni lazima niingie katika malango ya Kuzimu; \q nimenyang'anywa miaka iliyonibakia."
sw.R: Nilisema, "Nimefika nusu tu ya maisha yangu, nami ni lazima nipite katika malango ya Kuzimu. \q Miaka yangu iliyobaki imeondolewa kwangu."

vi.L: Tôi đã nói: "Giữa những ngày của đời tôi, tôi phải đi vào các cửa Âm Phủ; \q tôi bị mất phần còn lại của những năm tháng tôi."
vi.B: Tôi đã nói: "Đời tôi mới đến nửa chừng mà tôi đã phải vào các cửa Âm Phủ; \q tôi bị cướp mất những năm còn lại của mình."
vi.R: Tôi đã nói: "Tôi mới sống được nửa đời người, mà đã phải đi qua các cửa của nơi người chết. \q Những năm còn lại của tôi đã bị cất mất."

ko.L: 내가 말했다. "내 날들의 중간에 내가 스올의 문들로 들어가야 하는구나. \q 내 남은 햇수를 빼앗겼다."
ko.B: 내가 말했다. "한창때에 내가 스올의 문으로 들어가야 하는구나. \q 남은 내 햇수를 빼앗겼다."
ko.R: 내가 말했다. "내 인생이 겨우 절반 지났는데, 나는 죽은 사람들이 있는 곳의 문으로 들어가야 한다. \q 내 남은 햇수를 다 빼앗겼다."

pt.L: Eu disse: "No meio dos meus dias tenho de entrar pelas portas do Sheol; \q estou privado do resto dos meus anos."
pt.B: Eu disse: "Na metade da vida tenho de passar pelas portas do mundo dos mortos; \q os anos que ainda me restavam me são roubados."
pt.R: Eu disse: "Estou só na metade da minha vida e já tenho de passar pelas portas do mundo dos mortos. \q O resto dos meus anos me foi tirado."

decisions.choice: in the middle of my days: halfway through a normal lifespan
alternatives: in the quiet of my days
in the prime of my life
decisions.reason: The rare word may mean half or middle, or it may mean quiet or rest ("in the calm of my days"). Either way Hezekiah thinks he is dying too young; he was about forty at the time (2 Kings 18:2).

decisions.choice: I am deprived of: the rest of my life is taken away
alternatives: I am consigned for the rest of my years
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to appoint or to number. In this passive form it can mean "I am missing" (deprived) or "I am consigned" (to the gates of Sheol for my remaining years).

decisions.choice: the gates of Sheol: the entrance to the world of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead, pictured as a city with gates that close behind those who enter (Job 38:17; Psalm 9:14).

decisions.choice: Hezekiah says "tôi" in the poem
decisions.reason: The poem is a written psalm of lament and thanks; as in the published Psalms, the singer says "tôi" and speaks to God as "Ngài", while Hezekiah's spoken prayer in verse 3 keeps "con", as in 2 Kings 20:3.

decisions.choice: o Sheol (L); o mundo dos mortos (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Old Testament terms set it and as Isaiah keeps it through the book: Literal keeps the name "Sheol", and Balanced and Readable say "o mundo dos mortos", the place of the dead (m3). "A sepultura", which the English Readable's "grave" suggests, is one person's tomb; "o inferno" says something else. Verse 18 follows the same wording.
